doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Composing by pencil versus computer and the music trance
summary: Longo now uses a computer as paper but recalls writing a Dizzy-commissioned suite in a seven-week music trance.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I bet you had to play on some questionable pianos.
Oh are you kidding? I played on some dogs man. Now I don’t.
Right. Well as long as you brought up your composing, are you a paper guy or a computer guy now?

I’m a computer guy now but I use it as a paper. I don’t — I hear the music in my head and just use the computer. Because like when you used to — like if you wanted to repeat a section you’d have to write it. Now you just cut and paste and all that, and I can put all five saxophones and see what’s going on — now I think I’ll put that — and before you used to have to write all that. But I will say, look over there, look at all those arrangements.
Those are all arrangements man, that I used to do by hand. And some of those are more soulful than the computer.
That’s — I’d like to follow-up on that because when you have a pencil and you’re making a decision it seems like there’s some extra thought in there before you actually put it down.
Because you actually know you’re going to have to use an eraser to fix it if it doesn’t work.
So there’s pros and cons to both I guess.

Well now I’m used to the computer, but when I did the pencil I would go into — the best way to describe it — a music trance. And I’d be writing like that. Because I remember Dizzy commissioned me to write a three-movement suite. It was originally for the London Philharmonic with him. I wrote from ten in the morning to four AM, seven days a week for seven weeks. And I swear to God the time went by like, holy, it’s that late already, and I’d get a few hours sleep. And when I got finished I had a gig in Fort Lauderdale to play and I said man, I haven’t touched the piano in seven weeks. And I went down there and played great. And I told Moody, James Moody, about it and he said, © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

“Well that’s ‘cause where your head was at when you were writing that piece of music.” But I was in a music trance if you can understand, like you’re in a place. And the music is unfolding in your ear and you’re just writing it down like you’re taking dictation you know.
